messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem fitting a beta
parts:
On Monday, 19 March 2012 19:02:51 UTC+1, Virgilio Gómez-Rubio wrote:
Many thanks for your replies. It may be a good idea to report NA's in summary.fitted.values Also,
I set family=beta in the call to inla(), so I supposed that inla() knew that my responses are beta
distributed...

Yes, in principle, inla should know what link function to apply.  Unfortunately, this interacts in a bad way with the way models with multiple likelihoods are implemented currently; for multiple likelihood, the data vector becomes a matrix, where each column corresponds to its own likelihood (and hence link function).  The problem is then that the "NA values" in the matrix are doing double duty; for each row, typically there would be either an NA in one column and an observation in the other, _or_ NA in both.  In the former case, the NA would normally mean "no data because this row of the model belongs to the other likelihood.  In the latter case, the same holds, but no the _other_ NA means "missing value", and inla has no way of knowing which is which.  In theory, inla could then just apply the link functions on _all_ NA values, but that could quickly run into practical and numerical difficulties due to different scaling etc.  Hence, inla leaves it to the user to apply the link functions corresponding to NA elements, since the user does know the meaning of each NA entry.

A more elegant solution would be to have separate formulas and data vectors for each likelihood, but that would be a major redesign of the code, and so that won't happen overnight...
But I've designed a way for the user to instead specify specifically which elements come from which likelihood; I'll discuss it with Håvard.

/Finn L
